metadata.title: What teachers can do to enhance students’ well-being: Discussion

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This article is a discussion/review of studies included in a special issue and does not report an original ILSA micro-data analysis. Therefore, there is no analytic sample construction from PISA microdata, and no student/school sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures are described. For any future empirical work using PISA microdata, analysts should apply the complex survey design weights provided in the international database (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) to account for stratification and clustering. The manuscript does not specify which weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) would be used, because it does not conduct weighted estimation itself.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is not an empirical ILSA micro-data study predicting PV-based achievement outcomes; it synthesizes and discusses findings from multiple included papers. As a result, plausible values (PV) generation/combination and missing-data handling strategies for PV-based scores are not applicable to the discussion itself. The manuscript also does not provide an imputation or missing-data protocol because it does not run a new statistical model on ILSA microdata.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The article does not define an analytic subsample from a single ILSA dataset. Instead, it summarizes characteristics and results of multiple studies in the special issue, including some that use PISA 2018 (e.g., 58 or 67 countries) and reports sample sizes at the study level (e.g., total sample sizes for included studies), without providing a unified student-level analytic dataset or filtering rules.

data.outcome_summary: This article is a discussion piece that synthesizes evidence from studies in a special issue on student well-being and the role of teaching. It does not conduct an original machine-learning analysis, nor does it estimate predictive models on PISA microdata; instead, it reviews how included studies conceptualize well-being (e.g., hedonic/eudaimonic, social belonging) and how they relate teacher- or teaching-related variables to well-being outcomes. The manuscript highlights that several included studies use large PISA datasets (e.g., PISA 2018 with hundreds of thousands of students across many countries) and that methodological approaches in the included papers include longitudinal designs and multilevel analyses, but it does not report ML model performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) for any single predictive task. Limitations discussed focus on common-method bias from student self-reports, cross-sectional designs, and the lack of intervention evidence for causal mechanisms.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the manuscript is a narrative discussion/review rather than an empirical ILSA-based ML paper. It does not provide a single dataset/cycle/grade/domain used for a new analysis, does not report an analytic sample with per-country counts, and does not specify PV handling, missing-data handling, or ML algorithms with performance metrics. Consequently, fields required for predictive ML extraction (main_findings, ml_techniques, and sample breakdown) are intentionally left empty/null per the schema rules for review articles.
